gloss: to become old; to grow worn; to age

definitions.gloss: to become old, to grow worn, to age, to look dated
definitions.explanation: To show signs of age and use. Describes objects, buildings, or styles that have become worn, faded, or outdated over time.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}びた{本|ほん}を{開|ひら}く。
この{建物|たてもの}はだいぶ{古|ふる}びてきた。
examples.english: This building has aged quite a bit.

examples.japanese: {古|ふる}びた{写真|しゃしん}を{眺|なが}めていると、あの{頃|ころ}のことを{思|おも}い{出|だ}す。
examples.english: When I gaze at the old, faded photographs, I remember those days.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{古|ふる}びた{建物|たてもの} (aged building)
・{古|ふる}びた{本|ほん} (worn old book)
・{古|ふる}びた{町並|まちな}み (old, weathered townscape)
・{古|ふる}びない (not age, remain timeless)

USAGE NOTES:
Most commonly used in the past participle form {古|ふる}びた as a modifier. While it describes aging and wear, it does not necessarily carry a negative connotation — it can evoke a sense of nostalgia, character, or charm. The negative form {古|ふる}びない is used to praise things that remain fresh or timeless despite the passage of time.
